newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - No increase in govt liabilities - Canberra.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - No increase in govt liabilities - Canberra.

text.p: Australian Finance Minister John Fahey said on Thursday the government would not increase its liabilities.

"The Treasurer (Peter Costello) has made it clear that the government will not be increasing its liabilities," Fahey told parliament, referring to a suggest that the government issue redeemable preference shares in telecommunications group Telstra Corp rather than privatising it.
"The treasurer has also made it clear that the government will manage existing liabilities in the most cost-effective way."
Fahey had been asked about the government's response to independent senator Brian Harradine's proposed alternative to the partial sale of state telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp.
Harradine has proposed the government issue redeemable preference shares in Telstra rather than sell one-third of the carrier.
Costello told parliament on Wednesday the proposal had no attraction for the government and would increase Canberra's liabilities.
Harradine and fellow independent Mal Colston are crucial to the sell-off legislation passing the upper house Senate, where the government is two seats short of a majority.
